subject.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)

question: Should OpenClaw treat a full-line unnamespaced `<invoke name="…">…</invoke>` block as disposable tool-call leakage, or preserve it unless it carries an `antml:`/`mm:` namespace or an unambiguous wrapper?
rationale: Current source establishes an allow-listed tag-recognition approach, while this patch newly makes bare XML destructive on both delivery and persistence paths; source inspection cannot determine whether that compatibility break is intentional.

options.title: Scope bare stripping to unambiguous cases
options.body: Keep `antml:`/`mm:` support and strip bare invokes only when a wrapper or other established discriminator proves they are degraded tool calls.

options.title: Adopt bare invoke as reserved markup
options.body: Accept deletion of legitimate full-line bare XML examples and document that unnamespaced invoke blocks are reserved for sanitizer removal.

recommendation.title: Scope bare stripping to unambiguous cases
recommendation.body: Keep `antml:`/`mm:` support and strip bare invokes only when a wrapper or other established discriminator proves they are degraded tool calls.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the current repair implementation and can apply the selected boundary, though final API and compatibility direction requires repository maintainer approval.
